original_request.text:
为一个现有的团队项目管理 Web 应用增加项目内任务管理功能。

团队成员需要能够在项目中创建任务、编辑任务标题和描述、指定负责人、设置截止日期、更新任务状态（待办、进行中、已完成），并按状态筛选任务。

完整交付需要包含数据持久化、服务端 API、前端交互界面和自动化验证。

需要考虑现有项目的身份认证和权限机制，但不得擅自设计一套新的用户账户系统。

技术栈、数据库和现有 API 结构尚未提供，不得虚构这些技术事实。将必要的未知条件明确标记为待确认事项。

en.original_request_translation:
Add project-level task management to an existing team project management web application.

Team members need to create tasks within a project; edit task titles and descriptions; assign an owner; set a due date; update task status (To do, In progress, Done); and filter tasks by status.

The complete delivery must include data persistence, a server API, a frontend interface, and automated verification.

Account for the existing project’s authentication and authorization mechanisms, but do not design a new user account system.

The technology stack, database, and existing API structure have not been provided. Do not invent these technical facts. Mark necessary unknowns explicitly as items to confirm.

items.title: Deliver project-level task management
items.context_problem: The request is to add project-level task management to an existing team project management web application. The technology stack, database, and API structure are unknown; the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms must be used.
items.outcome: Team members can manage tasks within a project; the complete feature is integration-verified and documented for developers, using the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms.
items.scope: Coordinate data persistence, server API, frontend interaction, integration verification, and developer documentation. Confirm and adapt to the existing technology stack, database, API, and authentication/authorization mechanisms before implementation.
items.non_goals: Do not create a new account system; do not assume or specify an unprovided technology stack, database, or API structure; do not include task management outside projects.
acceptance_criteria: Project members can create tasks and edit their titles, descriptions, owners, due dates, and statuses.
Task statuses include To do, In progress, and Done, and tasks can be filtered by status.
Task data is persisted and provided through a server API.
The frontend uses the server API and follows the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms.
Automated verification covers key task-management behavior and integration paths; developer documentation explains usage and verification.
items.verification: Use integration automation to check core task flows, status filtering, persistence, and permission boundaries; review developer documentation for usage and verification guidance.

items.title: Implement the task domain model and persistence
items.context_problem: The request is to add project-level task management to an existing team project management web application. The technology stack, database, and API structure are unknown; the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms must be used.
items.outcome: Task data can be persisted in the existing application data layer, with project association, title, description, owner, due date, and the three statuses.
items.scope: After confirming existing data-layer conventions, define the task data structure and persistence capabilities needed to create, read, and update tasks.
items.non_goals: Do not choose an unconfirmed database or migration technology; do not implement a new user account or authentication system; do not own the HTTP API or frontend.
acceptance_criteria: A task record can be associated with a project and stores its title, description, owner, due date, and To do/In progress/Done status.
The persistence layer supports creating, reading, and updating tasks, and data remains available after an application restart.
Data constraints and owner references follow the confirmed existing data model and permission mechanisms.
items.verification: Run automated checks for the data structure and persistence operations, confirming field mapping, project association, status constraints, and persistence.

items.title: Implement the project task management server API
items.context_problem: The request is to add project-level task management to an existing team project management web application. The technology stack, database, and API structure are unknown; the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms must be used.
items.outcome: Clients can manage project tasks through server endpoints that follow the existing API conventions and are protected by the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms.
items.scope: Following the confirmed API and authentication/authorization patterns, implement endpoints for task creation, reading/updating, and status filtering, using the task persistence capability.
items.non_goals: Do not design a new account system; do not invent an API style, routes, or authentication approach; do not implement the frontend.
acceptance_criteria: The API supports creating and reading tasks within a project.
The API supports updating task titles, descriptions, owners, due dates, and statuses.
The API supports filtering by To do, In progress, and Done status.
The API reuses existing authentication and project permission checks and rejects unauthorized requests according to existing conventions.
Requests and responses follow the confirmed API structure and use task persistence correctly.
items.verification: Use server-side automated checks for valid and invalid input, create/update/filter operations, and authorized and unauthorized access.

items.title: Implement the project task management frontend
items.context_problem: The request is to add project-level task management to an existing team project management web application. The technology stack, database, and API structure are unknown; the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms must be used.
items.outcome: Team members can create, view, and edit tasks and filter them by status in the project interface.
items.scope: Within existing frontend patterns, implement the task list, create/edit interactions, owner and due-date inputs, status updates, and filtering; connect to the task API.
items.non_goals: Do not introduce an unconfirmed frontend technology or design system; do not bypass server-side permissions; do not implement the server API.
acceptance_criteria: The project interface displays tasks and provides an entry point for creating a task.
Users can edit task titles, descriptions, owners, due dates, and statuses.
Status choices include To do, In progress, and Done, and the list can be filtered by status.
The interface reads and submits data through the confirmed API contract and presents success or failure results.
items.verification: Use frontend automation to cover task creation/editing, status updates, status filtering, and API success/failure feedback.

items.title: Verify task management integration and write developer documentation
items.context_problem: The request is to add project-level task management to an existing team project management web application. The technology stack, database, and API structure are unknown; the existing authentication and authorization mechanisms must be used.
items.outcome: Key end-to-end project task-management paths can be verified automatically, and developers can understand the feature and verification approach from its documentation.
items.scope: Integrate the related data-layer, API, and frontend work; document the feature overview, integration with existing authentication/permissions, and how to run automated verification.
items.non_goals: Do not take ownership of implementing each layer’s feature; do not add unconfirmed technical facts or a new account design.
acceptance_criteria: Automated integration verification covers task creation, task field/status updates, status filtering, and persistence round trips.
Verification covers how the existing authentication and project authorization mechanisms constrain task operations.
Developer documentation describes the feature, existing authentication/permission integration points, and how to run the relevant automated verification.
Integration verification and documentation are based on confirmed project technology and API facts, without invented details.
items.verification: Run integration automation and review the documentation for key paths, permission behavior, and verification commands.

relationships.rationale: Task persistence is part of delivering complete project-level task management; the parent item owns overall acceptance.
The server-side task API is part of delivering the complete project-level task-management feature; the parent item owns overall acceptance.
The frontend task interactions are part of delivering complete project-level task management; the parent item owns overall acceptance.
Integration verification and developer documentation make delivery of the complete feature verifiable; the parent item owns overall acceptance.
API read/write acceptance depends on available task data persistence.
The complete frontend task-management flow depends on an available, confirmed task API contract.
End-to-end integration verification depends on the task persistence implementation.
End-to-end integration verification depends on the server-side task API.
End-to-end user-flow verification depends on the frontend task interactions.
